newsitem.title: USA: U.S. May light vehicle sales decline 5.8 percent.
newsitem.headline: U.S. May light vehicle sales decline 5.8 percent.

text.p: U.S. car and light truck sales during the month of May totaled 1,406,649 units, according to reports from all major automakers, marking a 5.8 percent decline from the 1,492,529 units sold a year earlier.

The seasonally adjusted annual sales rate for the month was 14.8 million units, down from 15.4 million units a year earlier, but an improvement from the 14.3 million units reported in April. The rate is calculated with seasonal factors supplied by the U.S. Commerce Department.
Automakers sold 640,163 North American-built cars in the United States in May, down 13.7 percent from a year ago.
The seasonally adjusted annual rate for domestic cars was 6.65 million units, compared with 7.56 million in May 1996 and 6.48 million in April.

Automakers sold 579,959 domestic trucks in the United States during May, off 0.1 percent from a year earlier. The seasonally adjusted annual sales rate for domestic trucks was 6.2 million units, compared with 6.01 million a year earlier and 5.87 million in April.

Imported car sales totaled 132,265 units, up 0.8 percent from a year ago, with a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 1.38 million units. Imported truck sales rose 39.7 percent to 54,263 units for an annual sales rate of 610,000 units.
For the 1997 year to date, automakers have sold 6.33 million vehicles, down 1 percent from the 6.44 million they sold a year earler.
